key_insight: PPMem gives video world models a compact, persistent 3D memory using plane primitives, so generated scenes can retain structure over time instead of treating each frame independently. This helps the model remember and reuse dominant scene elements like walls, floors, and facades with very few parameters.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of durable 3D memory in scalable video world models, which makes long-horizon generation and scene consistency difficult. It aims to store and update scene geometry efficiently while generating videos of indoor and outdoor environments.
method: Represents persistent scene memory with plane primitives, where each primitive uses only 7 parameters.
Integrates this planar memory into a video diffusion transformer to condition generation on accumulated 3D structure.
Uses the memory to capture dominant scene surfaces and maintain spatial consistency across extended video generation.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a more efficient way to build video world models that are structurally consistent and scalable. It can improve long-term scene coherence, reduce redundant representation costs, and support more realistic environment generation and exploration.
